body.statement:
For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), put
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4,
 \qquad
 M_{k,\ell}=M_A+M_B.                                      \tag{18}
\]
The design-A and design-B coarse structural-mode enumerations used by \(\mathscr A\) have at most \(M_A\) and \(M_B\) templates, respectively.  Every template has a semialgebraic description with at most
\[
 N_0=4\ell+10k+12,
 \qquad
 S_0=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1),
 \qquad
 D_0=4                                                     \tag{19}
\]
variables, polynomial sign atoms, and polynomial degree.

Let \(\mathsf{Comp}\), \(\mathsf{Proj}\), and \(\mathsf{Lab}\) be coordinatewise nondecreasing versions of the explicit published output-format bounds for, respectively, the connected-component-description and sampling algorithm, the subsequent one-block projection and realizability algorithm, and the real-univariate, Thom-sign, and root-isolation algorithms invoked in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\).  A component record uses the original ambient variables and at most one real-univariate primitive-element coordinate for its sample; projection retains only the two target variables.  Define the bounds sequentially by
\[
 (A_C,S_C,D_C)=\mathsf{Comp}(N_0,S_0,D_0),
 \qquad
 Q_C=(N_0+3,S_C+3,2D_C+2),                                \tag{20}
\]
\[
 (A_P,S_P,D_P)=\mathsf{Proj}(Q_C;2),
 \qquad
 Q_P=(2,S_P,D_P),
 \qquad
 (A_L,D_L)=\mathsf{Lab}(Q_P),                             \tag{21}
\]
and
\[
 B_{k,\ell}
 =M_{k,\ell}
  (2+A_C+N_0+S_C+D_C)
  (1+A_P+2+S_P+D_P)
  (1+A_L+D_L).                                             \tag{22}
\]
Then \(B_{k,\ell}\) is explicit and computable and bounds both the total number of labeled outputs and every real-univariate algebraic degree produced by the compiler.  If \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\) and \(\operatorname{Exp}_2(x)=2^x\), the published bounds imply, for a universal constant \(C\ge1\), the conservative envelope
\[
 B_{k,\ell}
 \le
 \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(
   \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(CQ^C\right)
 \right).                                                  \tag{23}
\]

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  For rational input coordinates of numerator and denominator binary length at most \(L\), let \(\mathsf{Comp}_h\), \(\mathsf{Proj}_h\), and \(\mathsf{Lab}_h\) denote the corresponding published integer-coefficient height bounds, and define
\[
 h_0=B_{k,\ell}(L+1),\qquad
 h_C=\mathsf{Comp}_h(N_0,S_0,D_0,h_0),\qquad
 h_P=\mathsf{Proj}_h(Q_C,h_C),\qquad
 H_{k,\ell}(L)=\mathsf{Lab}_h(Q_P,h_P).                    \tag{24}
\]
After clearing guarded denominators, every algebraic target certificate can be represented by a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(B_{k,\ell}\), together with rational isolating endpoints whose coefficients and endpoints have binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  A Turing implementation therefore terminates.  Enlarging the same universal constant in (23) if necessary, the composed published height bounds give
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le
 \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(
   \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(CQ^C\right)
 \right)
 (L+1)^{\operatorname{Exp}_2(\operatorname{Exp}_2(CQ^C))}.\tag{25}
\]
The classification first enumerates the structural charts of \(\mathscr A\), then describes their connected components, and only then performs target projection and labeling; it does not report a generic two-copy quantifier-elimination test.
body.justification: The corrected theorem separates exact causal template counts from sequentially composed published component, projection, labeling, degree, and rational-height bounds.
body.gap: A generic decidability assertion neither counts the causal templates nor propagates one algorithm's output format into the next algorithm's input.
body.consumer: Symbolic implementations obtain an honest fixed-alphabet termination and exact-encoding contract over both oracle-real and rational input tiers.
body.proof_tex:
We verify (18)--(25) in the order in which the compiler executes them.

First consider the purely structural count.  A normalized nonnegative vector \(b_i\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}\) has a nonempty support, hence at most \(2^{\ell}-1\) possible labeled supports.  The four shared response vertices therefore contribute at most
\[
 (2^{\ell}-1)^4.                                           \tag{26}
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\), a rank-two cell has two orientations.  Since \(v_e(z)>0\), the two nonnegative incident coefficients that sum to \(v_e(z)\) have exactly three support states at a fixed \(z\): left zero, right zero, or both positive.  Thus the rank-two modes contribute at most \(2\cdot3^k\) templates per cell.  The same theorem gives \(3^k\) coordinatewise split faces in mode \(\mathrm E\), together with the three modes \(\mathrm L\), \(\mathrm R\), and \(\mathrm D\).  Hence the number of local templates, allowing either observable rank, is at most
\[
 2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3.                               \tag{27}
\]
There are four response-cycle cells.  Multiplying (26) by the fourth power of (27) proves the formula for \(M_A\).

For design B, the residual-forest refinement in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) assigns to each of the four response links either the zero-residual state or an active state with one of \(k-1\) lexicographically first pivots and one of two pivot signs.  This gives
\[
 1+2(k-1)=2k-1                                             \tag{28}
\]
states per link.  Relevance is certified by a pair of distinct instrument values and a sign.  There are
\[
 2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1)                                     \tag{29}
\]
such signed witnesses.  Multiplying \(M_A\), the fourth power of (28), and (29) proves the formula for \(M_B\).  Adding the two design-specific counts, rather than taking their maximum, proves (18).  Endpoint incidences and sign atoms not fixed by a structural template remain polynomial sign conditions inside that template; their sign-invariant pieces and connected components are therefore counted by the later factors in (22).

We next establish the uniform input format (19).  Retaining all four endpoint vectors uses \(4\ell\) coordinates, and retaining both incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells uses \(8k\) coordinates.  In design B, the projective or common-instrument coordinates and the optional \(q^X\) auxiliaries use at most \(2k\) further coordinates; population margins, response masses, four residual-transfer scalars, and normalizations use at most twelve more.  Thus the number of coordinates is at most \(N_0=4\ell+10k+12\).

There are \(4k\ell\) table equations.  Endpoint simplex and support atoms contribute at most \(4\ell+4\), and coefficient simplex, zero-pattern, and split-face atoms contribute at most \(24k+8\).  Residual definitions and transfer equations contribute at most \(16k+8\); even if all proportionality minors are retained in place of transfer variables they contribute at most \(4(k-1)^2\).  Shared-instrument equations, margin and response-mass normalizations, endpoint-incidence atoms, cycle consistency, and all signed relevance candidates contribute fewer than
\[
 20(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1)
\]
additional atoms.  Adding these displayed bounds and using \(k\ge2\) and \(\ell\ge3\) gives at most \(S_0=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1)\) atoms.

The table equations are bilinear.  A residual \(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0)\) has degree at most two.  Introducing one transfer scalar on each active residual link writes negative proportionality as transfer equations of degree at most three, while the only four-link cycle equation is the product of four transfer scalars and has degree four.  Shared-instrument equations have degree two, and the relevance polynomial has degree at most three when \(q^X\) is retained.  Simplex, support, normalization, and incidence atoms have no larger degree.  Consequently all atoms have degree at most \(D_0=4\).  This proves (19) without using a constructed property as an assumption.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) to one template of format \((N_0,S_0,D_0)\).  By the definition of \(\mathsf{Comp}\), it returns at most \(A_C\) component records, each described in the original \(N_0\) ambient variables, with its sample encoded by at most one real-univariate primitive-element coordinate, using at most \(S_C\) atoms of degree at most \(D_C\).  The accepted one-copy compiler then adjoins two target coordinates, the two graph equations \(t=\tau_C\), and the single different-target condition.  Clearing the denominators in the sampled target coordinates raises degree by at most a factor two and adds at most two.  Its next input is therefore bounded by
\[
 Q_C=(N_0+3,S_C+3,2D_C+2),                                \tag{30}
\]
which is the first sequential substitution in (20).  Applying the cited one-block projection and realizability bound to (30), retaining the two target coordinates, yields the tuple in (21).  Applying the cited real-univariate, Thom-sign, comparison, and rational-root-isolation bounds to that actual two-variable projection output gives \(\mathsf{Lab}(Q_P)\).  Thus one initial structural template produces at most \(A_CA_PA_L\) final labels.  Across both designs the number is at most
\[
 M_{k,\ell}A_CA_PA_L\le B_{k,\ell}.                       \tag{31}
\]
Each degree occurring at the three stages is at most the corresponding positive factor in (22), and hence at most their product \(B_{k,\ell}\).  Equations (30)--(31) prove the count and degree claims.  Crucially, both the chart multiplier and the output of the preceding stage enter the next bound; no maximum of an initial chart count and an unrelated per-chart bound is used.

The published bounds recorded in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}coarse\text{-}envelope}\) are explicit in the numbers of variables and sign polynomials and their degrees.  Substitute (19) first into the component bound, substitute the resulting description format through (30) into the projection bound, and finally substitute (21) into the labeling bound.  Here \(N_0=O(k+\ell)\), \(S_0=O(Q)\), \(D_0=4\), the ambient dimension remains at most \(N_0+3\) through component evaluation and projection, and the structural multiplier in (18) is at most exponential in a polynomial in \(Q\).  The cited stagewise bounds therefore show after these three sequential substitutions that every factor of (22) is bounded by
\[
 \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(
   \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(C_0Q^{C_0}\right)
 \right)                                                  \tag{32}
\]
for one universal \(C_0\).  A fixed product of positive quantities satisfying (32), together with \(M_{k,\ell}\), is bounded by the same form after increasing the universal constant.  This proves (23), including the necessary \(k^2\) term and the two properly nested exponentials.

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), every chart coefficient belongs to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\): normalization divides only by the positive selected margins, and every chart division uses a pivot whose nonzero sign is recorded in that chart.  There are finitely many templates by (18), and each of the three algorithmic stages terminates by \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  Hence the complete field-relative computation terminates.

Suppose now that the coordinates of \(\zeta\) are rational with numerator and denominator length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing the deleted simplex coordinates, forming the selected margins, and forming \(T_e=p_e/r_e\) use only a fixed-alphabet number of additions and guarded divisions.  Clearing denominators by recorded positive factors, or by their squares when only nonvanishing is known, preserves every sign condition.  The resulting integer-coefficient chart formula has coefficient length at most the conservative initial height \(h_0=B_{k,\ell}(L+1)\).  The integer height part of the cited component algorithm gives \(h_C\); feeding that actual height and (30) into the projection bound gives \(h_P\); feeding the resulting projection format and height into root isolation and labeling gives exactly \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\) in (24).  This sequential composition proves the asserted coefficient and isolating-endpoint bound.  The cited square-free factorization and root-isolation procedures provide the square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval, and the degree conclusion follows from (22).

For fixed \((k,\ell)\), the integer height bounds in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}coarse\text{-}envelope}\) are polynomial in the incoming height, with exponents and coefficients controlled by their corresponding format bounds.  Substituting the format envelope (23) successively into the three height maps in (24), and enlarging the universal constant once, gives (25).  All loops now have finite bounds and all integer operations are effective, so the rational-input Turing implementation terminates.

Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) establishes that the structural templates are enumerated before component descriptions, that target projection occurs only after the components have been described, and that target variation is tested by a one-copy refinement.  The causal meaning and legal lifted outputs of that classification are supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:full\text{-}rigidity\text{-}atlas}\).  Therefore the procedure bounded above is the causal structural compiler \(\mathscr A\), not generic two-copy quantifier elimination.
